entries.definition: relating to general ideas rather than particular physical examples
entries.example: The teacher connected the abstract idea with an everyday decision.

entries.definition: specific and clearly described rather than general
entries.example: A concrete example made the argument easier to examine.

entries.definition: relating to the ideas used to organize understanding
entries.example: The diagram provides a conceptual framework for the discussion.

entries.definition: examining parts and relationships carefully
entries.example: The analytical section explains why the two approaches differ.

entries.definition: giving an account of what something is like
entries.example: The descriptive paragraph reports what the students observed.

entries.definition: intended to make reasons or processes understandable
entries.example: The explanatory note shows how the total was calculated.

entries.definition: examining two or more things in relation to each other
entries.example: The comparative study uses the same questions in both locations.

entries.definition: concerned with experiences or qualities rather than numerical measurement alone
entries.example: The qualitative interviews explored how residents understood the change.

entries.definition: concerned with amounts expressed as numbers
entries.example: The quantitative table records the number of completed journeys.

entries.definition: using methods for examining patterns in numerical data
entries.example: The statistical summary includes the variation as well as the average.

entries.definition: the principles and organized methods used in an investigation
entries.example: The methodology explains why these questions and participants were chosen.

entries.definition: an established sequence of actions for a task
entries.example: The procedure requires a check before any data is replaced.

entries.definition: an agreed set of rules for carrying out a particular activity
entries.example: The interview protocol protects participants’ choice not to answer.

entries.definition: a value or condition defining how a model or process operates
entries.example: Changing one parameter altered the model’s prediction.

entries.definition: a measure or sign used to understand a wider condition
entries.example: Attendance is one indicator of use, not a complete measure of learning.

entries.definition: a reference standard used for comparison
entries.example: The earlier test provides a benchmark for the new system.

entries.definition: an initial condition or measurement used for later comparison
entries.example: We measured the baseline before changing the instructions.

entries.definition: a level at which a condition or rule begins to apply
entries.example: The report explains why that threshold was chosen.

entries.definition: a limit that restricts possible choices
entries.example: Limited storage is a constraint that the design must respect.

entries.definition: the boundaries of what an activity or investigation covers
entries.example: The scope includes local journeys but not long-distance travel.

entries.definition: a restriction that affects what can be achieved or concluded
entries.example: The small sample is a limitation that readers should know about.

entries.definition: the importance or meaning of a finding or event
entries.example: The discussion explains the practical significance of the result.

entries.definition: an explanation of what information means
entries.example: The interpretation changes when we consider the missing records.

entries.definition: the final result of an activity or process
entries.example: The outcome was a usable guide, not simply a longer document.

entries.definition: a result discovered through an investigation
entries.example: The most useful finding concerned a problem no one had predicted.

entries.definition: guided by relevant evidence rather than unsupported assumption
entries.example: An evidence-based decision states which observations support it.

entries.definition: a reference identifying the source of quoted or discussed information
entries.example: The citation allows readers to locate the original study.

entries.definition: details that identify a source used in a piece of work
entries.example: Check the reference before claiming that a source supports the statement.

entries.definition: a list of sources used or consulted for a piece of work
entries.example: The bibliography includes the books and reports consulted.

entries.definition: words repeated exactly from a source
entries.example: The quotation should preserve the speaker’s actual wording.

entries.definition: identifying who created or supplied an idea or work
entries.example: Clear attribution distinguishes the writer’s ideas from another person’s contribution.

entries.definition: presenting another person’s words or ideas as your own without acknowledgment
entries.example: The workshop explains how note-taking habits can help prevent plagiarism.

entries.definition: the quality of offering an independently created idea or expression
entries.example: The task values originality without rewarding unsupported claims.

entries.definition: the introduction of a useful new idea, method, or product
entries.example: The innovation solved a small problem that users had repeatedly reported.

entries.definition: the ability to produce useful or interesting new ideas
entries.example: Constraints can encourage creativity when the goal remains clear.

entries.definition: a desire to learn or discover more
entries.example: Her curiosity turned an ordinary photograph into a research question.

entries.definition: the ability to begin useful action without waiting to be told
entries.example: He showed initiative by asking users where the guide was unclear.

entries.definition: a plan or suggestion presented for consideration
entries.example: The proposal includes an aim, a method, and a realistic budget.

entries.definition: the reasons underlying a choice or action
entries.example: The rationale explains why interviews were more suitable than a quick poll.

entries.definition: a short description of the main parts of a subject
entries.example: The overview helps readers understand how the sections fit together.

entries.definition: extra supporting material placed after the main text
entries.example: The appendix contains the questions used in the survey.

entries.definition: additional material that supports the main work
entries.example: The audio supplement provides another way to study the dialogue.

entries.definition: a central claim developed and supported in a piece of writing
entries.example: The essay’s thesis appears clearly near the end of the introduction.

entries.definition: a long research document written for an academic qualification
entries.example: Her dissertation examines how public spaces are used after dark.

entries.definition: a student studying toward a first university degree
entries.example: The undergraduate joined a supervised community research project.

entries.definition: relating to study after a first university degree
entries.example: The postgraduate course requires more independent research.

entries.definition: an established organization with a particular public or social purpose
entries.example: The institution publishes clear information about its admission requirements.

entries.definition: combining knowledge or methods from different fields
entries.example: The interdisciplinary project connects design, history, and environmental science.

entries.definition: used to contrast two different facts or situations
entries.example: The first method records numbers, whereas the second explores personal experiences.

entries.definition: at a later time after an event already mentioned
entries.example: The team tested the prototype and subsequently revised the instructions.
